descriptions.text: Jude has grown up among the faerie nobility since being taken from the human world as a child. She wants a place at court despite the contempt directed at mortals, especially by Prince Cardan. Proving herself draws her into political schemes where belonging and safety are not the same thing. As rivalries threaten her sisters, Jude must decide how far she is willing to go to gain influence in a society that was never meant to welcome her.

descriptions.text: Scarlett's chance to visit Caraval arrives just as an arranged marriage seems to close off the life she wants. Finding her means entering a contest whose appearances cannot be trusted. The promise that it is only a game offers little comfort when her sister's future seems to depend on winning.

descriptions.text: De dieren van een boerderij komen in opstand tegen de boer die hen verwaarloost. Onder leiding van de varkens proberen zij het werk en de opbrengsten voortaan eerlijker te verdelen. Hun nieuwe samenleving begint met de belofte dat de vroegere ongelijkheid zal verdwijnen. De fabel volgt hoe een gezamenlijk ideaal onder druk komt te staan wanneer enkelen steeds meer macht krijgen.

descriptions.text: A reporter listens as robot psychologist Susan Calvin recalls incidents from the development of robotics. The linked stories consider the ways people interpret machines and the difficulties that arise when expectations meet unfamiliar behaviour. Different situations place responsibility, judgment and the relationship between humans and robots under pressure. Read together, the accounts build a fictional history of a technology whose significance depends as much on the people around it as on its own capabilities.

descriptions.text: In een reeks verbonden verhalen onderzoekt Isaac Asimov hoe mensen en robots met elkaar omgaan. Een journalist luistert naar de ervaringen van robotpsycholoog Susan Calvin, die terugblikt op gebeurtenissen uit de ontwikkeling van de robotica. De afzonderlijke situaties stellen telkens andere vragen over gedrag, verantwoordelijkheid en de verwachtingen die mensen van hun machines hebben. Samen vormen de verhalen een geschiedenis van een technologie waarvan de maatschappelijke betekenis niet losstaat van menselijke keuzes.

descriptions.text: Hercule Poirot's quiet retirement in King's Abbot is interrupted when the wealthy Roger Ackroyd is found murdered. The death follows that of a local widow, and rumours already connect the people around them. Doctor Sheppard becomes involved as the detective examines a household full of possible motives. What residents choose to say can be as important as what they know. The investigation asks how an apparently familiar village can conceal events that its neighbours have failed to understand.

descriptions.text: In a future America controlled by a military dictatorship, an annual walking competition pushes its participants toward their physical limits. Continuing the contest becomes harder as exhaustion and psychological pressure accumulate. The event places individual endurance inside a system defined by obedience and state power. First published under Stephen King's Richard Bachman pseudonym, the novel uses the demands of the walk to examine a society willing to make extreme suffering part of an organised public competition.

descriptions.text: In een toekomstig Amerika onder een militair en totalitair bewind vindt ieder jaar een uitputtende wandelwedstrijd plaats. De deelnemers moeten blijven doorgaan terwijl de lichamelijke en psychische druk oploopt. Wat als een afgebakende competitie begint, maakt steeds sterker zichtbaar hoeveel macht de organisatoren over hun levens hebben. Stephen King schreef deze dystopische roman onder de naam Richard Bachman. De wedstrijd vormt het uitgangspunt voor een verhaal over uithoudingsvermogen en een samenleving die mensen aan extreme eisen onderwerpt.

descriptions.text: Robert Graves presents imperial Rome through a fictional account written by Claudius himself. Dismissed by his relatives because of physical disabilities, Claudius observes a ruling family shaped by rivalry, ambition and the threat of poisoning. The reigns of Augustus, Tiberius and Caligula become the setting for his precarious survival. His position at the edge of power offers an unusual view of those who wield it, before events bring him unexpectedly to the imperial throne.

descriptions.text: Santiago Nasar is murdered in a small town despite widespread knowledge of the threat against him. Years later, a returning investigator tries to reconstruct the circumstances from accounts that do not agree. The question is not simply who carried out the killing, but how so many people could know about it without preventing it. Gabriel García Márquez turns the reconstruction into an examination of shared responsibility, public judgment and the uncertain evidence left by memory.

descriptions.text: In Depression-era Minnesota, Odie lives under harsh authority at the Lincoln Indian Training School. descriptions.text: Tan Yunxian grows up learning medicine from her grandmother in fifteenth-century China. Her friendship with a girl training as a midwife gives that education a shared purpose. Marriage threatens both: the expectations of her new household restrict whom she may see and how she may help other women. Inspired by a historical physician, the novel follows the conflict between Yunxian's abilities and the boundaries placed around her life, with female friendship central to her choices.
